provenance.l: MER EDL reconstruction (NASA) — Opportunity entry 5,700 m/s inertial at −11.5°, 840 kg design mass, β 89.8 kg/m²; chute 250.3 s at 7.52 km, RAD firing 336.3 s at 127 m, ~13.8 m/s airbag impact; bridle cut 6.9 m (reconstructed, preliminary)

Opportunity landing (Astronomy.com, a secondary source) — 26 bounces and about 200 m of bouncing and rolling into Eagle crater (22 m across). First bounce height and time to rest are not published: drawn as Spirit’s, an estimate

MER landing press kit (Jan 2004) — heat shield 20 s after the chute; 20 m bridle spooled out 10 s after it; radar lock about 2.4 km; airbags at 284 m, 8 s before impact (Spirit plan); airbag retraction from 12 min after landing for about an hour, petals open from L+96 min (plan figure, Spirit)
